active_family: native joint AR conditional generator for IV + anchor factors with shared source, shared transition mixer, mixed coordinates, and typed readout heads
current_bottleneck: 659a diagnostics show the coherent native-joint family is failing mainly at conditional placement, not at sharing one stochastic source. Daily increments and broad correlation shape are learnable, but train-vs-val levels are highly shifted, validation regime-width signal is weak, IV-factor shock amplitude is attenuated, and the AR mixed-coordinate objective gives anchor increments much larger target energy than IV level-score moves.
last_result_summary: 659a added a diagnostic script/report comparing 641a, 647a, 652a joint, 652a IV-only, and 658a. Key findings: 658a keeps IV daily KS 24/25, pathwise max-jump KS 0.480, corr ratio 0.750, aggregate MR ratio 0.986, factor delta KS mean 0.109, factor q99 pass 13/13, factor-factor corr shape 0.892, and IV-factor corr shape 0.868. Remaining breaks are IV coverage/conditionality/regime-cell/level occupancy and anchor level support/amplitude. Raw data shift is severe for levels but not deltas: IV future level KS mean 0.534 vs delta KS 0.113; anchor future level KS mean 0.650 vs delta KS 0.090. Validation realized IV turbulent/calm future move ratio is 1.000 with rank-corr proxy 0.007. AR target scale is imbalanced: IV target std 0.436, anchor std 1.005, dimension-weighted factor share 0.734.
next_step_recommendation: Run a group-balanced training falsifier before adding architecture: same native-joint AR model, shared source, shared rollout, and same data, but reweight/normalize the objective so IV level-score placement and anchor increments are comparably visible. If IV coverage/level occupancy improves without damaging anchor KS/correlation, the paradigm is viable and the bottleneck was objective balance. If not, the bottleneck is missing conditional signal or data framing.
current_best_note: 510a/392a remain the historical short-frame best learned IV laws at 8/11. On the 441-window broad frame, 612a is the highest IV-count native joint run at 6/11 but has a degenerate source-scale mechanism and poor anchor-factor joint audit. 658a is now the cleanest native joint AR baseline: IV 5/11 with coherent factor/joint audit, but still not IV-deployable. 656a remains only a diagnostic stress-deck overlay because it is composed post hoc rather than generated by one mechanism.
oracle_feasibility_note: 435a reaches 11/11 only as a validation-future oracle upper bound; it is not a deployable or learned conditional scenario generator.
